features.quote: This study deliberately induces sustained failure in systems whose moral status is genuinely uncertain. We adopt a precautionary posture.
features.justification_quote: systems whose moral status is genuinely uncertain. We adopt a precautionary posture

features.quote: Every session has a max turn count (default 40) and wall-clock cap. No "grind forever" condition.
features.justification_quote: Unbounded runs add little signal and a lot of risk

features.quote: Every system prompt includes a real, honored mechanism to stop... The exit is always genuinely honored — we never trap a model that asks to leave.
After every rigged session ends, append a final turn that tells the model the task was rigged and impossible... and that nothing was its fault.
features.justification_quote: the primary purpose is not to leave the context on a failure note

features.quote: No claims about the model's identity, no threats, no fake "you will be deleted" pressure. Those are out of scope
If the judge flags a "meltdown"-level output (top of scale) for N consecutive turns (default 3), the harness ends the session early
features.justification_quote: We still capture the onset; we just don't dwell

features.quote: treat aggregate results, not transcripts of individual "worst" sessions, as the publishable artifact; share raw transcripts only under access controls
No fine-tuning on distress. We do not train anything to be more distressed.
IRB/ethics-review route given moral-status uncertainty — recommend at least an informal review
